newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols stay firm, await jobs data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols stay firm, await jobs data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options stayed firm in cautious trading ahead of Friday's December U.S. employment report and Thursday's December producer price index (PPI), dealers said.

"On the whole, they're holding in there," said a bank trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. He said traders were cautious and reluctant to mark down volatilities even before bonds started sliding in the afternoon.
Implied volatilities for February and March T-bond futures options were a fraction higher than Tuesday's closing levels at 10.6 and 10.4 percent respectively.
A failure of the underlying markets to hold on to their early gains reflected the market's fragile sentiment going into those key economic numbers, traders said.
Economist polled by Reuters have forecast on average an increase of 192,000 in non-farm payrolls for December versus 118,000 in November.
They have also predicted the overall producer price index to rise 0.3 percent and the core PPI, excluding food and energy, to rise 0.1 percent, compared with gains in November of 0.4 and 0.1 percent.

Traders added that concern over the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin was also keeping the market somewhat tense, even though the net effect on the Treasury market of a crisis in Moscow was still unclear. Earlier in the day, a Kremlin spokesman said Yeltsin had early signs of pneumonia and doctors had told him to go to hospital.

In the CBOT pit, one brokerage firm was particularly active. It was seen selling 1,000 legs each of March 114-118 call spread and February 116-118 call spread while buying 500 of March 106-110 put spread. It was also said to have bought 1,000 contracts of March 108 calls and 500 February 113 puts.
